# aeneid-014 review (Aeneid II.486-587), two passes

Findings: **major 5, medium 21, low 27**. Changes made by script to `units.json` (52 `l`/`i`/`n` fields in 33 units, plus `about`; `t`, `ln`, `p`, `v` and the `l`/`i` line counts checked unchanged against the original) and 6 entries added to `scan-fixes.json`. Speech marks: five speeches, 5 opening and 5 closing marks in each of `t`, `l`, `i` after the repairs below. The ” at 520, 524 and 550 heads the next unit's `t` by design and is carried at the end of the previous unit's `l` and `i` (u18, u21, u33); u21 and u33 lacked it and u34's `l` had it at the wrong end (fixed, items 18-20).

## Changes to units.json
Major
1. u16 (512-514) n: "'Aedibus in mediis' puts the preposition between adjective and noun" is false; the order is noun, preposition, adjective. Fixed.
2. u23 (526-528) n: "'natorum' is the old contracted genitive plural" is false; it is the ordinary genitive plural of natus. Fixed.
3. u15 (507-511) `i`, `l`, `n`: `desueta` agrees with `arma` ("arms long disused"), not with `senior`; the `i` ("the old man, long unused to arms") and the `l` ("arms long unaccustomed the old man") made the old man the one unaccustomed. Reworded in all three; note now says `desueta` agrees with `arma`.
4. u44 (567-570) n: the Servius/Varius/Tucca remark and "missing from the best manuscripts" are unverifiable here. Removed; the note keeps only what Greenough's bracketing shows.
5. u50 (583-587) n/l/i: `merentis` was called "the participle used as a noun, 'those who deserve it'" with `poenas` left unconstructed; `sumere poenas` takes the penalty as object, so the noun reading cannot stand. Now: participle of `mereo`, accusative plural in Greenough's -is agreeing with `poenas`, "deserved penalties" (cf. `sceleratas poenas` 576); the genitive-singular alternative ("the penalty of one who deserves it") is named and set aside. `l` "exacted of the deserving" and `i` "from one who deserves it" changed to match.

Medium
6. u16 n: "'aetheris' is a Greek genitive" is wrong (genitive of aether). Fixed. Also added: `umbra` is an ablative of means.
7. u18 (518-520) n: `sumptis iuvenalibus armis` is a plain ablative absolute, not "loosely"; fixed.
8. u25 (531-532) `l`: "much life with blood" put `multo` on `vitam`; it belongs to `sanguine`. Now "life with much blood".
9. u28 (540-541) `l`: "such toward an enemy was Priam" made Priam the subject. Now "such toward an enemy, Priam, he was".
10. u30 (544-546) `l`: "from the top of the shield in vain by the boss hung" mistranslated `e summo clipei... umbone pependit`. Now "from the shield's topmost, in vain, boss it hung".
11. u41 (562-563) n: "The three sentences are built the same way: the three objects of tender concern" is wrong (three subjects of `subiit`, not sentences, not objects). Fixed.
12. u43 (565-566) `i`: "flung their bodies from the roof" adds "roof", which is not in the Latin. Now "to the ground in a leap".
13. u11 (501-502) n: `nurus` glossed "(and daughters)"; it is daughters-in-law only. Fixed.
14. u47 (577-580) n, `l`, `i`: Mycenae "ancestral", "patrias... loosely used for the 'ancestral' cities: Sparta (Menelaus') and Mycenae (Agamemnon's)" not supportable from the Latin. Now "her country's Mycenae" in `l` and `i`; note says `patrias` agrees with `Mycenas`.
15. u47 n: "the Latin Library 'patris'... bring in Tyndareus alone" was speculation; now only "a singular, 'her father's'".
16. u48 (581) `l`, `i`, n: `occiderit... arserit` called "perfect subjunctives" while the `l` rendered them as future perfects ("Will have fallen"); the form is both. Note now says future perfect (also the perfect-subjunctive form); `l` "Troy burned" to "Troy will have burned"; `i` had an invented "And all the while" and no verb for the question: now "Is Priam to have died by the sword, Troy to have burned in fire?".
17. u49 (582) n: same label for `sudarit` fixed.
18. u21 (523-524) `l`, `i`: closing ” missing (Hecuba's second speech ends at 524; the mark heads u22's `t`). Added.
19. u33 (550) `l`, `i`: closing ” missing (Pyrrhus' speech ends at "morere."). Added; note says the mark is carried here.
20. u34 (550-553) `l`: carried the ” at its start though `t` has it and the speech is closed in u33. Removed from `l`.
21. u12 (503-505) n: "Priam had fifty sons, each with a chamber in the palace" is not in the Latin and unverifiable here. Replaced by a statement of what `thalami` and `spes nepotum` mean.
22. u9 (496-499) n: "compare Iliad 5 and 11 for rivers in spate" cannot be verified here. Removed.
23. Scan-fix 2.495 (see below).
24. Scan-fix 2.510.
25. Scan-fix 2.545.
26. Scan-fix 2.572.

Low
27. u1 n: "although the sentence began with the plural 'aedes'" misleading; reworded (the plural belongs to the preceding clause).
28. u6 n: "'postes' here means the leaves or jambs of the door" unverifiable; now "the same word as at 490".
29. u7 n: "a play on sound" made specific (alliteration, via vi).
30. u19 n: tautology "'tempus' is the crisis of the time" removed.
31. u22 n: the object `eum`/`longaevum` explanation was muddled; `longaevum` is the object of `locavit`, serving `recepit`.
32. u24 n: `manu` "in his hand" to ablative of means, "with his hand".
33. u30 n: `rauco aere` "ablative of cause" to means.
34. u30 n: "'et' would add a word but not change the sense" removed (`e summo` and `et summo` do differ); now "we follow Greenough".
35. u31 n: "Priam is told to go as a messenger to the underworld" unsupported as stated; now says he is to go to Achilles and, being about to be killed, the message goes to the dead.
36. u32 n: added that Pyrrhus speaks of himself in the third person.
37. u35 n: "The first half of a famous passage" removed.
38. u38 n: "not having been frightened until this sight of a king's death" removed (an inference the Latin does not give).
39. u45 n: `sibi infestos` "dative of reference" to "a dative with the adjective".
40. u50 n: Latin Library `haec` "would reverse the sense" unverifiable; now "a different word; we follow Greenough".
41. u15 `l`: "As" for `uti` to "When" (matches the note).
42. u16 n: "household gods, whose images are mentioned at 517" (identification unsupported) removed.
43. u16 n: `umbra` ablative (added, see 6).
44. u11 `i` (echo): "fouling with his blood the very fires he had himself hallowed" is a close echo of familiar versions; now "staining with his blood the flames he had himself consecrated" (and the same in `about`).
45. u16 `i` (echo): "beneath the open vault of heaven" to "out in the open under the bare sky".
46. u17 `i` (echo): "doves driven headlong by a black storm" to "doves that a black storm has sent plunging down".
47. u18 `i` (echo): "What dreadful resolve, my poor husband" to "What dreadful notion, most unhappy husband".
48. u27 `i` (echo): "if there is any justice in heaven that cares about such things" to "if heaven holds any sense of right that cares for such things".
49. u34 `i` (echo): "slipping in the pools of his son's blood" to "slipping in a great deal of his son's blood".
50. u30 `i` (echo): "a spear that had no war in it" to "a spear that was no weapon of war".
51. Scan-fix 2.519 (syllabification only).

## Checked and left
- Homer: the only cites are "Iliad 24" (u29) and "the last book of the Iliad" (u28), both at book level and consistent with the Latin (the ransom of the body); no line cites remain.
- Every other grammatical label read against its form: `ululant` plural with `aedes` (u0), `amplexae` and `effata` (present sense), `postis`/`omnis`/`ignis`/`hostis`/`Penatis` accusatives in -is, `procubuere`/`Deseruere`/`misere`/`dedere`/`Exarsere` (-ere = -erunt), `moriere` (-ere = -eris), `adforet` for `adesset`, `pependit` from pendeo, `Pelidae` Greek-form dative, `Tyndarida` Greek accusative, `Iliadum` Greek genitive plural, `Atridas`, `memento` future imperative, `sudarit` syncopated, `Creüsa` three syllables, `super... eram` tmesis, `capulo tenus`, `circumstetit` with accusative: all true.
- `l` word by word against the Latin and `l`/`i` agreement for every unit: checked; apart from the units above, fine. 
- Packet disagreements with the Latin Library (491, 507, 517, 529, 539, 542, 546, 558, 561, 562, 569, 572, 579, 584, 585, 587): notes only where the sense changes (569, 572, 579, 584, 587), as drafted.
- Refused: stating `merentis` as the noun "'those who deserve'" with `poenas`. `sumere poenas` takes `poenas` as its object, so a second accusative noun for the people punished does not parse; see item 5.

## Scansion
I scanned all 102 lines by hand (quantities of every open syllable, not only the flagged ones), because the scanner leaves open syllables to the metre and so can return a valid fit with wrong quantities. Six entries added (all pass the validator's rules: letters of `sc` equal the words, six feet, foot patterns):
- 2.495 (late loca): lātē (long -ē) and lŏcă; the scanner had la-te short, lo-ca long. im-mis | si Dă-nă(i) | et lā | tē lŏ-că | mī-lĭ-tĕ | com-plent.
- 2.510 (nequiquam umeris): nē-quī-quam long-long-long, -quam elided, ŭ-mĕ-rīs; the scanner had ne-qui short and umeris with long u- and me-.
- 2.545 (coniecit): consonantal i, con-jē-cit, three syllables; the scanner read four.
- 2.572 (Danaum, coniugis): Dă-nă-um (um elided before et); the scanner took Da-naum with long Da-.
- 2.519 (coniunx) and 2.579 (coniugiumque): syllabification only (con-iunx; con-ju-gi-um), quantities already right, as 2.200 and 2.444.

Hand-scanned, scanner right, no entry (notable): 2.563 (the flagged line: et dī | rep-ta dŏ | mūs et | par-vī | cā-sus Iu | li; `mus` is lengthened in arsis at the caesura after `domus`, the only fit, cost 2.8 explained), 2.492 ariete (ar-je-te, consonantal i), 2.512 Aedibus (Ae one syllable), 2.513 iuxta (final -ā long), 2.514 umbra (ablative, long -ā), 2.526 (elapsus; `de` long at the diaeresis after the fourth foot, forced), 2.531 evasit, 2.538 (coram with a long first syllable is the only fit, cost 0.6), 2.557 Asiae/Iacet, 2.562 Creüsa (Cre-ü-sa), 2.567 Iamque (consonantal i, Iam long by position), 2.571 Teucros (Teu one syllable), 2.573 Erinys (-ri- long, forced at line end), 2.581 Priamus, 2.585 extinxisse (division ex-tin-xis-se versus ex-tinx-is-se, same weights; left), 2.496 spumeus amnis (no elision of -us, as the scanner never elides a syllable ending in -s: correct), 2.522 tempus eget (same), 2.509 desueta (de-su short, the only fit).
